header: Date: 2027-03-09 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Location: Zoom | Redwood: Olivia Park (AE), Daniel Ruiz (SE) | Quantum Bridge: Maya Singh, Tom Reeves, Lina Zhao, Arjun Patel
summary: Discovery call for reserved GPU capacity. Customer evaluating dedicated vs hosted vs private. Main concerns: predictable latency, isolation for multi-tenant inference, burst handling (prewarm/hot pool), KMS integration and SOC2 compliance. Agreed to share pricing, run burst sims, and reconvene for VPC/On-prem deep-dive.
topics: Requirements for isolation and data residency
transcript:
[00:00] Olivia (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, we'll run through your current stack and what you want from reserved capacity. I'm Olivia, AE at Redwood, and Dan (Daniel) is our SE.
[00:22] Maya (QB): Hi, Maya here, Head of ML. We run 2 models — one conversational and one reranker for search. Latency is main thing for UX.
[00:40] Tom (QB): Tom, infra. We currently self-host GPUs on GCP, mixed preemptible and reserved. Trying to understand if reserved with Redwood Dedicated reduces ops overhang.
[01:05] Daniel (SE): Great, quick clarification, when you say reserved, do you mean dedicated pods we spin up in our infra or Redwood hosts the pool for you? We support Hosted, Dedicated (reserved GPU pool on Redwood infra), and Private (VPC/on-prem).
[01:30] Tom: We're open to both Dedicated hosted and Private VPC. Data residency and KMS integration matter; health data, so logs need retention and auditability.
[01:48] Lina (QB): Also need to confirm we can pin model versions for canary rollouts and have audit trails for each inference.
[02:10] Olivia: Absolutely, model pinning and rollout policies are supported. Quick question on traffic — can you sketch avg qps and burst 95th/99th?
[02:28] Maya: Sure, baseline convo model ~120 qps avg during peak hours, bursts up to 600 qps for short windows (1-3 minutes) — p95 generation latency budget 250ms, p99 600ms. Reranker is lower fps but tight tail.
[02:55] Daniel: That p99 of 600ms is doable with dedicated GPU pools but we need to size prewarm/hotpool. We usually advise a hot-pool combined with prefix KV cache to shave start-up cost — sorry, KV cash? I mean KV cache.
[03:18] Tom: (laughs) Yeah we've seen "KV cash" in older notes. On prewarm, what's Redwood's typical warm-up time for a cold model?
[03:34] Daniel: Cold start depends on quantization and model size; for a 7B-ish conversational model, warm from zero to hot in ~25-40s if you need weights loaded, but hot-pool or checkpointed snapshots reduce that to sub-2s for new requests.
[03:58] Maya: Okay, latency numbers are helpful. Cost trade-offs matter — we'll balance the reserved monthly commit vs occasional bursts. How does burst accounting work? Do you bill separate for burst or consume reserved capacity first?
[04:18] Olivia: Our reserved contracts include a baseline committed capacity; bursts can be handled via burst credits or on-demand capacity at a premium. We can model multiple burst policies — including guaranteed burst allocation for X minutes per month or pay-as-you-go overage.
[04:40] Arjun (QB): Any options for soft limits or tenant shaping? We want to protect core production traffic if a heavy batch job goes nuts.
[04:55] Daniel: Yes, shard-level QoS and tenant fencing are standard. You can set per-route token quotas and throttle non-critical workloads. We also do graceful degradation — auto-fallback to smaller model variants if the primary is constrained.
[05:18] Lina: For Private/VPC, how does KMS integration look? We use Cloud KMS and have an HSM for keys; need server-side encryption and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[05:33] Daniel: Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. We integrate via standard key wrapping for model artifacts and logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 export. There are options for retention windows to meet compliance.
[05:49] Tom: Do you support bring-your-own-image or do we use Redwood runtime images? We have tightly-curated containers.
[06:04] Olivia: For Private on-prem you'd bring your images; for Dedicated hosted we provide optimized runtime images but allow models you provide. There's also a private-control-plane option so you can manage deployments.
[06:22] Maya: On the burst sim — we want to run synthetic traces that mimic our production diurnal and sudden spikes. Can Redwood run that for sizing?
[06:35] Daniel: Yes, we have a burst-simulation harness. If you share token-level histograms and a 1-week trace, we can model prewarm and hot-pool sizing and give a recommended committed instance count and expected p95/p99 tail under your load.
[06:52] Maya: Great. One of our concerns is eviction and eviction tolerance. If GPUs are preempted in cloud, how do we guarantee model slot stickiness?
[07:08] Daniel: For Dedicated hosted, we use a reservation layer with protected nodes that avoid preemption. For Private/on-prem that's up to your infra; we provide the orchestration with graceful checkpointing to minimize lost KV cache. We also offer cold-fanout mitigation strategies so that a sudden surge doesn't hammer your upstream DBs.
[07:34] Olivia: Another note — our billing granularity is per-second with per-token accounting layered on top for generation. That gives you predictable unit economics for both baseline and burst.
[07:49] Arjun: Helpful. Security quick question: SSO and RBAC — we need SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO for the console and API tokens management.
[08:03] Daniel: Supported — SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and audit logs with per-token attribution. We also integrate with enterprise IdPs.
[08:17] Lina: Does Redwood store raw prompt data for hosted modes? That's a compliance red flag for us.
[08:27] Olivia: By default hosted has short-term logs for debug but there are options for no-persist and request-level encryption; for strict data policies we recommend Private or Dedicated with VPC so logs never leave your environment.
[08:45] Tom: Let's talk scale numbers. If we commit to say 40 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved, what headroom do we get for bursts and what's typical latency SLO hit?
[09:02] Daniel: It depends on batching and sequence length. If your seq lengths are 128 tokens avg and batching is used, 40 A100s should handle your baseline and modest bursts; for 600 qps spikes you'll want a hotpool equivalent of ~8-12 instances kept warm depending on model size. We'll put numbers in the burst sim.
[09:26] Maya: We saw weird peaks when marketing releases new features. Can auto-scaling respond fast enough (less than 60s)?
[09:36] Daniel: Auto-scaling has a lower bound because spin-up takes time; that's why hot-pool and prewarming are recommended for short sharp bursts. For longer sustained increases (>5 min) autoscale is effective.
[09:52] Olivia: Also, we can provide a hybrid approach — baseline reserved + a small hot-pool and rapid on-demand to cover unknowns.
[10:06] Arjun: Regarding canary deploys, how easy is rollback and audit?
[10:15] Daniel: Canary rollouts are first-class — you can route X% traffic to new model, inspect outputs, and roll back. All requests are traced and stored in the audit logs if you enable that.
[10:30] Maya: Any concerns with tokenization differences between our current tokenizer and Redwood runtime?
[10:38] Daniel: We support pluggable tokenizers and can run a compatibility pass. There are sometimes tokenization edge-cases that affect cost; we typically do a pass in the POC.
[10:52] Tom: On networking — for VPC private, do you support private peering and egress controls?
[10:59] Olivia: Yes, VPC peering, restricted egress, and customer-managed NAT are supported on Private deployments.
[11:12] Lina: For compliance we'll need SOC2 docs and a pen-test report.
[11:19] Olivia: We'll share SOC2/ISO artifacts and our recent pen-test summary. For Private we can also do an onsite compliance review if needed.
[11:31] Maya: Let's get a quick sketch of pricing structure — committed hourly for reserved and overage rates?
[11:38] Olivia: Generally reserved is a monthly/annual commit with tiered discounts; bursts are billed either by credits or on-demand at a higher rate. We'll send an example quote.
[11:50] Arjun: If we move to Redwood Dedicated hosted, can we request local region placement? Latency to EU users matters.
[11:58] Daniel: Yes we can provision capacity by region; we have multi-region support and can route users to closest region.
[12:07] Maya: (interruption) Sorry, quick — how does Redwood optimize kernels and quantization for different GPUs?
[12:15] Daniel: We do kernel selection and quantization recommendation automatically based on model architecture and sequence length distribution. For maximum perf we can recommend INT8/4-bit quant profiles and run internal evals.
[12:30] Tom: That helps. On the POC — how do we validate tail latency and correctness?
[12:38] Olivia: We typically run a 2-week POC: you supply traces and eval prompts; we run burst sims and end-to-end latency tests and share dashboards with token-level breakdowns.
[12:50] Maya: Sounds good. Any limitations on model sizes? We have some ~30B models later in roadmap.
[12:59] Daniel: We support larger models on Dedicated and Private; memory planning and multi-node sharding may be needed. We'll advise on quantization and sharding patterns.
[13:12] Arjun: For rollback under noisy neighbor conditions, is there an automated fallback to smaller variants?
[13:20] Daniel: Yes, we have policy-driven fallbacks where if latency SLOs break we route to a smaller variant or cached response.
[13:31] Tom: Ok let's drill into burst modeling specifics — what's the artifact you need?
[13:39] Daniel: Ideally token-level histograms per minute for 7 days, sequence length distributions, percent of generate vs embed vs rerank calls, and any time windows where latency is especially sensitive. A CSV is fine.
[13:55] Maya: We'll prepare that. On the contract side, can we get termination clauses and data deletion SLA?
[14:04] Olivia: Yes, we'll include standard termination language and data deletion commitments. For Private we can arrange on-prem data wipe procedures.
[14:17] Lina: Are there guardrails for batch ops so they don't preempt inference?
[14:25] Daniel: Yes — batch jobs can be scheduled on separate pools or assigned lower QoS so they don't evict inference lanes.
[14:34] Arjun: How do you do tracing into our APM for per-request observability?
[14:41] Daniel: We export traces via OpenTelemetry and have integrations with common APMs. You can attach request ids for end-to-end traces.
[14:52] Maya: Any real customer examples of handling marketing spikes?
[14:57] Olivia: We had a customer in fintech who used a hybrid reserved+hotpool approach — they kept a small hotpool and had burst credits for unusual spikes; p99 stayed within their SLA during product launches. We'll anonymize and share the case study.
[15:14] Tom: Ok, pricing + burst sim + SOC2 docs are our main asks. Anything else?
[15:21] Olivia: The SE deep-dive for VPC/on-prem and a POC plan. We'll propose dates in the follow-up.
[15:30] Maya: Works for us.
[15:36] Olivia: Quick housekeeping — will someone own internal signoffs?
[15:40] Maya: I'll own the ML signoff, Tom owns infra, Lina will handle compliance.
[15:48] Olivia: Great. We'll send the materials and set up the follow-up. Thanks all.
[15:55] (meeting ends)
